rule_metadata.description: The phonetic conversion of a non-vowelled Noon (نْ) or Tanween into a hidden Meem (مْ) sound with a 2-count nasal Ghunnah when followed by the letter Baa (ب).

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Iqlab literally means to turn or flip something around (التَّحْوِيل).
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: When a non-vowelled Noon (نْ) or Tanween is followed by the letter Baa (ب) across two words (or occasionally within a single word), the Noon sound is converted into a hidden Meem sound, accompanied by a 2-count nasal resonance (Ghunnah) and gentle lip contact.

trigger_letter.name: Baa
trigger_letter.mechanism: The tongue does not touch the upper gum line for Noon; instead, the lips close gently to form a light Meem sound before releasing into the Baa.

theoretical_foundation.mushaf_indicator: A small vertical or horizontal standing Meem (م) written directly above or in place of the Tanween or over the Noon Sakinah.
theoretical_foundation.duration_rules: The converted Meem sound must be held with nasalization (Ghunnah) for exactly 2 counts.

practical_examples.breakdown: The Noon Sakinah changes into a hidden Meem sound before Baa, held with a 2-count Ghunnah.
The Dammah Tanween on Samee'un converts into a Meem sound when meeting Baa.
Single-word Iqlab occurring between Noon and Baa inside the same word.
Kasrah Tanween on Kiraamin converts to Meem before Baa.
